title: The Verdict of Saint Alder's
premise: Vesper Dunmore, the unassuming concierge of Saint Alder's Grand Hotel, has a gift for reading people—and a private habit of solving deaths the police misfiled as accidents. When he investigates the disappearance of guest Miriam Ashe, her recovered diary keeps being written after the date she vanished, forcing him to conclude she is alive, hiding, and leaving him coded messages. Following a ledger disguised as the hotel's century-old guest register, Vesper uncovers that Saint Alder's founding families laundered a fortune through the hotel and that Miriam is the heir they tried to erase. In the end, Vesper exposes the conspiracy at the hotel's centennial gala, chooses truth over his own invisibility, and helps Miriam reclaim her identity—while accepting that he can never return to being unnoticed.
about_author: Ivo Pemberton is the pen name of a former night-shift hotel manager who spent a decade watching guests check in with secrets. He writes mysteries from a small flat above a shuttered seaside inn, where he still keeps the old ledgers for inspiration.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sees Everything
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV introduces his concierge work at Saint Alder's and his quiet history of solving three 'accidental' deaths. When police close the case of drowned guest Miriam Ashe, he notices her shoes were dry inside. Emotional beat: the tension between his talent and his need to stay invisible.

chapters.title: A Diary That Outlived Its Owner
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV: Miriam's sister delivers the recovered diary to the hotel. The final entry is dated three days after Miriam vanished, in handwriting Vesper recognizes as deliberately altered. Emotional beat: cold dread curdling into exhilaration—he was meant to find this.

chapters.title: The Register Nobody Reads
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV: cross-referencing diary dates against the hotel's antique guest register, he finds columns of numbers hidden in room assignments. Detective Inspector Corrane dismisses him as a busybody. Emotional beat: humiliation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Room 412 Speaks
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV: decoding the first ledger entries reveals payments routed through Room 412 every quarter since 1971. Night porter Edda warns him someone else has been asking about Miriam. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by first real fear.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Isn't Grieving
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Miriam's sister, Cressida, whose grief performance slips when she thinks no one watches. Vesper notices she wears Miriam's ring on the wrong hand. Emotional beat: suspicion—the family knows more than sorrow.

chapters.title: Founding Families
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV: hotel archives reveal four founding families; three surnames still appear on the board. The fourth—Ashe—was struck through in 1971. Emotional beat: the past pressing its weight onto the present.

chapters.title: Someone Searches My Rooms
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV: returning from his day off, he finds his quarters searched but nothing taken—a message, not a theft. He hides the diary pages in the lost-and-found ledger. Emotional beat: invisibility failing him for the first time.

chapters.title: The Porter's Confession
chapters.summary: Edda's POV: she reveals she saw Miriam alive the night of the disappearance, leaving through the service door with a man from Room 412. She stayed silent for thirty years of hush money. Emotional beat: guilt finally breaking open.

chapters.title: Ciphers in the Carpet
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV: the lobby carpet's border pattern matches the ledger numbers—a map of safe-deposit boxes beneath the hotel. Emotional beat: wonder at how plainly secrets hide, mirroring his own life.

chapters.title: Corrane Closes In
chapters.summary: Corrane's POV: the detective, uneasy about the Ashe case, reopens it and names Vesper a person of interest. Emotional beat: the law becoming an obstacle rather than an ally.

chapters.title: The Centennial Invitation
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV: the hotel announces its 100th-anniversary gala; the board orders all archives sealed. A note appears in his pocket: STOP ASKING. Emotional beat: threat made intimate and personal.

chapters.title: What Edda Buried
chapters.summary: Edda's POV: she gives Vesper a key she took in 1971 from the dying fourth-family patriarch. Emotional beat: passing the torch of an old sin to a new conscience.

chapters.title: Below the Lobby
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV: descending through the service tunnels, he opens deposit box 44 and finds cash, documents—and a recent photograph of Miriam, alive, dated last month. Emotional beat: hope igniting like a lit fuse.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Chapel
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV (first appearance): hiding as the hotel chapel's caretaker, she has been writing the diary deliberately, trusting only 'the concierge who sees everything' would follow it. Emotional beat: two invisibles recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV: she explains the founding families erased her grandmother's line to keep laundering money through the hotel; the ledger proves it. Emotional beat: identity as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Front Desk
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV: young porter Tam, whom he mentored, reports his movements to the board. Vesper realizes the trap closing around them both. Emotional beat: loyalty wounded by necessity.

chapters.title: The Gala Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge: the centennial gala, champagne, speeches by Chairman Alder-Voss. Vesper plants the ledger copies among the place cards. Emotional beat: calm surface over rising water.

chapters.title: Verdict Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV climax: during the toast, he reads the ledger aloud, and Miriam steps from the crowd to claim her name. Alder-Voss orders security; Corrane, arriving with warrants, must choose a side. Emotional beat: justice spoken outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Corrane's POV: arrests, a board member's confession, and the discovery that the 1971 'accident' was murder. Emotional beat: the law belatedly catching up to the truth.

chapters.title: What Vesper Owes
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV: offered a detective's position, he hesitates—exposure cost him the anonymity that kept him safe. Tam apologizes; forgiveness is given carefully. Emotional beat: reckoning with what visibility costs.

chapters.title: Checkout Time
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV: she signs the register as Miriam Ashe, restoring her family's line to the book, and offers Vesper a role as the hotel's investigator. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed, future opened.

chapters.title: The Concierge Remains
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV epilogue: he stays at the desk, watching new guests arrive with their secrets, the diary now shelved in the archive beside the ledger. Final line hints at a fresh anomaly in the register. Emotional beat: quiet satisfaction with one eye always open.
